name: issue-427-natvent-sleep-floor-churn
description: Issue #427 (rewritten post-#959, PROACTIVE_FLOOR removal): overnight WHF nat-vent session where indoor sits at exactly the same reading (66F) before and after the sleep window (22:00) begins. Before the sleep window, the reactivation gate (handle_door_window_open -> _nat_vent_reactivation_floor()) correctly refuses to restart free cooling at 66F because it's below the flat daytime comfort floor (68F). Once the sleep window begins, the SAME 66F reading correctly DOES restart free cooling, because the reactivation gate now resolves to the lower, sleep-aware floor (sleep_heat=64F) instead. This is the real, still-live regression surface #427 fixed -- previously the reactivation gate (and 4 other call sites unified under it by Issue #417) hardcoded the flat daytime floor with no sleep-window branch, so during the night a window reopening with indoor between sleep_heat and comfort_heat was wrongly refused reactivation. PROACTIVE_FLOOR (the mechanism the ORIGINAL version of this scenario tested) has since been fully removed (Issue #959) -- it was a different code path (a predictive ODE-based session-exit inside check_natural_vent_conditions), not the reactivation gate this rewrite covers.
notes: Issue #959 disposition: the original version of this scenario asserted an overnight session survived 4 re-evaluations without PROACTIVE_FLOOR tearing it down. PROACTIVE_FLOOR is now fully deleted from nat_vent_exit.py/automation.py, so that assertion would be vacuously true (there's no mechanism left that could fail it) -- it stopped being a real regression test the moment #959 shipped. This rewrite targets the surviving code _nat_vent_reactivation_floor() was actually written to fix, exercised through its real production call site (handle_door_window_open, automation.py), which is unrelated to and unaffected by the #959 removal.

Occupant impact (why this still matters): a resident who briefly closes a bedroom window overnight (checking on a kid, a noise outside, etc.) and reopens it relies on the system correctly judging whether it's still worth turning the fan back on. Before #427's fix, the system used the wrong (daytime) floor for that judgment overnight, incorrectly refusing to resume free cooling for hours after a brief window closure, even with plenty of thermal margin left before the real overnight floor (sleep_heat).

Config: comfort_heat=68F (daytime floor) vs sleep_heat=64F (overnight floor) -- kept several degrees apart, matching #427's original divergence. sleep_time=22:00, wake_time=06:30. No thermal_model supplied (confidence defaults to 'none'), which deliberately keeps handle_door_window_open's separate, still-live 'Phase 2 Guard 2' (thermal-model floor-imminence pre-activation skip) out of play -- that guard is NOT what #427/#959 concern and must not be allowed to interfere with or be mistaken for the mechanism under test here.

Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md Sec.10): (a) Scenario effectiveness: reverting _nat_vent_reactivation_floor() to unconditionally return comfort_heat (removing its sleep-window branch) makes the 22:05:01 assertion fail -- production_outcome_at would show the window staying paused (no natural_ventilation decision) since indoor(66) would no longer exceed the reactivation floor. (b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md's nat-vent reactivation-gate section should note the surviving call sites (handle_door_window_open plus 4 others) and that PROACTIVE_FLOOR's removal (#959) did not touch this function. (c) User outcome if this regresses: an overnight window reopening at a still-comfortable indoor temperature would incorrectly stay paused instead of resuming free cooling, costing the occupant hours of unnecessary HVAC energy use (or discomfort, if HVAC is off) for no real benefit -- silently, since nothing alerts them their window is open and the fan isn't running.
Promote to golden/ only after the user reviews and confirms this rewritten scenario per the Golden Simulation Test Policy (locked-golden files require explicit sign-off before modification).

events.note: Evening classification: mild day, hvac_mode=off. windows_recommended=true, but window_open_time is not set by this bare event, so handle_door_window_open()'s planned-window-period exemption does not short-circuit the reactivation gate below (matches the original #427 scenario's own precedent).
Before the sleep window (sleep_time=22:00). indoor=66F is BELOW the flat daytime comfort_heat floor (68F).

Window opens at 21:00, before the sleep window. _nat_vent_reactivation_floor() resolves to comfort_heat=68F (daytime branch). Gate check: indoor(66) > comfort_heat(68) is FALSE -- reactivation gate correctly refuses. Window-open falls through to the pause path instead of activating nat-vent.
Window closes -- resumes from the pause (nothing was running, so this is a no-op resume).
Now inside the sleep window (22:00-06:30 wraps midnight; 22:05 is unambiguously after sleep_time). SAME indoor/outdoor readings as 21:00 -- the only thing that changed is time-of-day.

Window reopens. _nat_vent_reactivation_floor() now resolves to sleep_heat=64F (sleep-window branch). Gate check: indoor(66) > comfort_heat(64) is TRUE, outdoor(58) < indoor(66) is TRUE, outdoor(58) < threshold(74+3=77) is TRUE, ceiling_ok (WHF fan_mode -> no ceiling check) is TRUE -- reactivation gate correctly activates nat-vent on the exact same temperature reading that was refused 65 minutes earlier.

Steady-state check: session remains active under normal conditions (no special mechanism required -- this just confirms nothing else in the pipeline destabilizes the session immediately after the sleep-floor reactivation).

assertions.reason: Before the sleep window, the reactivation gate uses the flat daytime comfort_heat (68F). indoor=66F is below it, so the gate correctly refuses to restart free cooling -- the window-open falls through to the pause path instead.
Window closes -- resumes cleanly (no nat-vent or fan was ever started).

Inside the sleep window, the SAME 66F reading now clears the reactivation gate because it resolves to the lower sleep_heat floor (64F) instead of the daytime comfort_heat (68F) -- this is the exact behavior #417/#427 fixed and #959 did not touch.
Session persists normally after the sleep-floor reactivation -- no unrelated mechanism destabilizes it.

verdict.summary: The nat-vent reactivation gate (handle_door_window_open -> _nat_vent_reactivation_floor()) correctly swaps from the flat daytime comfort floor to the lower, sleep-aware floor once the overnight sleep window begins -- proven by showing the identical 66F indoor reading refused before 22:00 and accepted after, isolating time-of-day as the only variable.
verdict.observed_behavior: 21:00:01 window-open with indoor=66F -> paused (gate refuses, daytime floor 68F). 22:05:01 window-open with the SAME indoor=66F -> natural_ventilation (gate accepts, sleep floor 64F). Session then persists normally.
verdict.expected_behavior: _nat_vent_reactivation_floor() resolves to sleep_heat during the configured sleep window and to comfort_heat otherwise, and every production call site that gates nat-vent reactivation (handle_door_window_open being the one this scenario exercises) must use that resolved value, not a hardcoded daytime constant.
